plan.author: pratos with Claude Code
plan.summary: Greenhouse has words for planning but none for the agent's own work, the live room, or the workspace where code changes. This plan names them, once, in the glossary and in `packages/schema`, so people, code and the agent say the same thing as the product grows onto pi-durable, Durable Objects and Containers. Library words stay inside the adapters that use them.
plan.current: The glossary has eight nouns across Planning and Identity (`docs/GLOSSARY.md`). It already contradicts itself in two places, and three of its schemas do not exist yet. The stack under it brings its own words, and many of them collide: *session* means six things across pi-durable, the Sandbox SDK and auth, *agent* is a configuration in pi-durable but an actor here, and Amp's *thread* is a unit of work while ours is a comment thread.
discoveries: Plan is defined as "a document" while banning *document* (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:28,30`), and Exploration is "an agent thread", which is not our Thread (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:23`).
The verb list omits Post, Record, Start and Report, which events already use (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:51`, `packages/domain/src/thread/decider.ts:10-13`).
`rationale` is read by the upcaster but is in neither the glossary nor the Decision schema (`packages/domain/src/upcast/index.ts:4-12`).
Chopin's product noun is *document*; *Plan* is its UI tab label, *room* is internal, and its hosted agent is the *Planner* (githubnext/chopin `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`).
Chopin calls what an exploration returns a *finding* (kinds research, spike, ask) and the one-sentence reason on a decision its *why* (`docs/decisions.md`).
pi-durable's *run* is the turns from one input to its final answer, the same as what people mean by the agent is running (pi-durable README, Concepts).
The Sandbox SDK 1.0 removed *sessions* and *preview URLs* as 0.x had them, so neither should become a domain word from that source.

The labels *decision report*, *option explorer*, *state machine explorer*, *trace views*, *parallel lookahead* and *pre-handoff exploration* do not appear in Maggie Appleton's talk or the Chopin sources. Her own terms are *boundary objects*, *interactive report*, *explore the terrain ahead of time* and *made meaningful contact with the important parts of reality*.
plan.endState: `docs/GLOSSARY.md` names four contexts with every noun, command and event the next phases of Greenhouse need, each entry with where the word was seen and the synonyms it replaces. Each noun has an Effect Schema in `packages/schema`. A translation table says which library word maps to which product word and where library words may appear. `just glossary-check` fails on a library word outside an adapter, an unknown verb, or a missing schema. `just glossary` renders the vocabulary as a map you can step through.
notDoing: Implementing Runs, Rooms or Workspaces. This plan names them; the deciders and screens are their own plans.
Renaming kernel words like Decider, Message and Rejection. They are the event-sourcing kernel's own words, internal to `packages/domain/src/kernel.ts`.
Adopting Chopin's identifiers. We borrow a word when users already say it, and leave Chopin's wire protocol where it is.
Rewriting the workshop page. Only the Appleton attribution is corrected, in the page and the viz-explainer skill.
plan.approach: Fix what the glossary already gets wrong before adding to it, so new words land on a consistent base. Then draw the contexts and the boundary, because the four decisions below are all about where a word lives. Write the entries and schemas next, then make the check enforce them, and finish by rendering the vocabulary so it can be shown and reviewed by looking.

plan.title: The domain vocabulary for a multiplayer coding agent
plan.author: pratos with Claude Code
plan.summary: Greenhouse has words for planning, but none for the agent's work, the live room, or the workspace. This plan names them in the glossary and `packages/schema`: pi-durable's words for agent work, Amp's *Thread* for a conversation with the agent, and *Comment* for today's comment thread.
plan.current: Eight nouns across two contexts; two definitions contradict themselves and three schemas are missing. The stack's own words collide: *session* means six things, pi-durable's *agent* is a configuration, and Amp's *thread* is our comment thread.
discoveries: Plan is "a document" while banning *document*, and four event verbs are missing from the verb list (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:28,51`).
`rationale` is read by the upcaster but named nowhere else (`packages/domain/src/upcast/index.ts`).
Chopin says *document* for the product, *Plan* only on a tab, *comment* in its interface and *finding* for research results.
pi-durable's *run* is one input to its final answer: what people mean by the agent is running.
Appleton's own terms are *boundary objects* and *interactive report*. The pattern labels on our workshop page are ours, not hers.
plan.endState: One glossary with four contexts, an adopted-words table pinned to pi-durable 1.4.0, a schema per noun, a check that enforces all of it, and a map of the vocabulary. After the workshop, the code says Comment.
notDoing: Implementing Runs, Rooms or Workspaces; this plan only names them.
Renaming kernel words like Decider and Message; they stay internal.
Copying Chopin's identifiers; we borrow only the words users already say.
Rewriting the workshop page beyond the Appleton attribution.

plan.title: The domain vocabulary for a multiplayer coding agent
plan.author: pratos with Claude Code
plan.summary: Greenhouse has words for planning, but none for the agent's work, the live room, or the workspace. This plan names them in the glossary and `packages/schema`: pi-durable's words for agent work, Amp's *Thread* for a conversation with the agent, and *Comment* for today's comment thread.
plan.current: Eight nouns across two contexts; two definitions contradict themselves and three schemas are missing. The stack's own words collide: *session* means six things, pi-durable's *agent* is a configuration, and Amp's *thread* is our comment thread.
discoveries: Plan is "a document" while banning *document*, and four event verbs are missing from the verb list (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:28,51`).
`rationale` is read by the upcaster but named nowhere else (`packages/domain/src/upcast/index.ts`).
Chopin says *document* for the product, *Plan* only on a tab, *comment* in its interface and *finding* for research results.
pi-durable's *run* is one input to its final answer: what people mean by the agent is running.
Appleton's own terms are *boundary objects* and *interactive report*. The pattern labels on our workshop page are ours, not hers.
plan.endState: One glossary with four contexts, an adopted-words table pinned to pi-durable 1.4.0, a schema per noun, a check that enforces all of it, and a map of the vocabulary. After the workshop, the code says Comment.
notDoing: Implementing Runs, Rooms or Workspaces; this plan only names them.
Renaming kernel words like Decider and Message; they stay internal.
Copying Chopin's identifiers; we borrow only the words users already say.
Rewriting the workshop page beyond the Appleton attribution.
plan.approach: Fix the glossary's mistakes first. Then add contexts, words and schemas, make the check enforce them, and render the map. Renaming code and stored events waits until after the workshop.

plan.summary: Greenhouse has words for planning, but none for the agent's work, the live room, or the workspace. This plan names them in the domain vocabulary and `packages/schema`: pi-durable's words for agent work, Amp's *Thread* for a conversation with the agent, and *Comment* for today's comment thread.
plan.current: Eight nouns across two contexts; two definitions contradict themselves and three schemas are missing. The stack's own words collide: *session* means six things, pi-durable's *agent* is a configuration, and Amp's *thread* is our comment thread.
discoveries: Plan is "a document" while banning *document*, and four event verbs are missing from the verb list (`docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md:28,51`).
`rationale` is read by the upcaster but named nowhere else (`packages/domain/src/upcast/index.ts`).
Chopin says *document* for the product, *Plan* only on a tab, *comment* in its interface and *finding* for research results.
pi-durable's *run* is one input to its final answer: what people mean by the agent is running.
Appleton's own terms are *boundary objects* and *interactive report*. The pattern labels on our workshop page are ours, not hers.
plan.endState: One domain vocabulary with four contexts, an adopted-words table pinned to pi-durable 1.4.0, a schema per noun, a check that enforces all of it, and a map of the vocabulary. After the workshop, the code says Comment.

Renaming kernel words like Decider and Message; they stay internal.
Copying Chopin's identifiers; we borrow only the words users already say.
Rewriting the workshop page beyond the Appleton attribution.

plan.title: The domain vocabulary for a multiplayer coding agent
plan.author: pratos with Claude Code
plan.summary: Greenhouse has words for planning, but none for the agent's work, the live room, or the workspace. This plan names them in the domain vocabulary and `packages/schema`: pi-durable's words for agent work, Amp's *Thread* for a conversation with the agent, and *Comment* for today's comment thread.
plan.current: Eight nouns across two contexts; two definitions contradict themselves and three schemas are missing. The stack's own words collide: *session* means six things, pi-durable's *agent* is a configuration, and Amp's *thread* is our comment thread.
discoveries: Plan is "a document" while banning *document*, and four event verbs are missing from the verb list (`docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md:28,51`).
`rationale` is read by the upcaster but named nowhere else (`packages/domain/src/upcast/index.ts`).
Chopin says *document* for the product, *Plan* only on a tab, *comment* in its interface and *finding* for research results.
pi-durable's *run* is one input to its final answer: what people mean by the agent is running.
Appleton's own terms are *boundary objects* and *interactive report*. The pattern labels on our workshop page are ours, not hers.
plan.endState: One domain vocabulary with four contexts, an adopted-words table pinned to pi-durable 1.4.0, a schema per noun, a check that enforces all of it, and a map of the vocabulary. After the workshop, the code says Comment.
notDoing: Implementing Runs, Rooms or Workspaces; this plan only names them.
Renaming kernel words like Decider and Message; they stay internal.
Copying Chopin's identifiers; we borrow only the words users already say.
Rewriting the workshop page beyond the Appleton attribution.

plan.title: The domain vocabulary for a multiplayer coding agent
plan.author: pratos with Claude Code
plan.summary: Greenhouse has words for planning, but none for the agent's work, the live room, or the workspace. This plan names them in the domain vocabulary and `packages/schema`: pi-durable's words for agent work, Amp's *Thread* for a conversation with the agent, and *Comment* for today's comment thread.
plan.current: Eight nouns across two contexts; two definitions contradict themselves and three schemas are missing. The stack's own words collide: *session* means six things, pi-durable's *agent* is a configuration, and Amp's *thread* is our comment thread.
discoveries: Plan is "a document" while banning *document*, and four event verbs are missing from the verb list (`docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md:28,51`).
`rationale` is read by the upcaster but named nowhere else (`packages/domain/src/upcast/index.ts`).
Chopin says *document* for the product, *Plan* only on a tab, *comment* in its interface and *finding* for research results.
pi-durable's *run* is one input to its final answer: what people mean by the agent is running.
Appleton's own terms are *boundary objects* and *interactive report*. The pattern labels on our workshop page are ours, not hers.
plan.endState: One domain vocabulary with four contexts, an adopted-words table pinned to pi-durable 1.4.0, a schema per noun, a check that enforces all of it, and a map of the vocabulary. After the workshop, the code says Comment.
notDoing: Implementing Runs, Rooms or Workspaces; this plan only names them.
Renaming kernel words like Decider and Message; they stay internal.
Copying Chopin's identifiers; we borrow only the words users already say.
Rewriting the workshop page beyond the Appleton attribution.
